habitat: Flocks in grassland within woodland, vleis, coastal plains and grassy riverbanks. It nests in ground burrows.
summary: A locally common resident, often more common in winter. Grey-brown cap and pale grey rump. The rump can look almost white. The rest of the upper parts are metallic blue, and the tail is deeply forked. In flight the call is a grating chaa. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: If the rump looks white, House Martin is told by the blue cap and the only slightly forked tail. Grey-rumped Swallow is more slender and more deeply forked, with a grey-brown cap.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^8=256 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 128–512.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: Grey-brown cap, not easily seen in flight.

upperparts.pattern: Metallic blue except the greyish cap and pale grey rump. The rump may look almost white.

calls.description: A grating chaa in flight. Grade A flight call from the Kafue floodplain, Zambia. The filename names Grey-rumped swallow.
